absent: Exact predicate logic of the sixty-four-kilobyte crossing test beyond its role as a DMA path selector.
DMA buffer allocation and release implementations for hardware and emulated paths.
RTC lock definition and CMOS byte access implementation.
Floppy DMA channel number and controller programming sequence.
Kernel FPU begin mask handling and interaction with preemption.
Register save implementation and trace event contents.
Signal frame conversion and regset query implementations.
Permission expansion handling and signal-handler locking protocol.
XSAVE runtime feature enumeration and supervisor state management.
Guest floating-point lifecycle and confidential-mode firmware contract.

findings.text: The floppy layer selects between emulated and physical channel handling through a chooser that consults a capability control. When automatic selection is active the chooser prefers emulation if the buffer resides beyond directly mapped memory or its bus translation reaches the twenty-four-bit ISA ceiling or the range straddles a sixty-four-kilobyte boundary, otherwise it prefers hardware. When automatic selection is inactive the choice follows the low bit of the capability control.

The emulated transfer initializer marks the programmed path active, remembers the target port and direction derived from the requested mode, stores the buffer start and length, clears any leftover residue count, and reports success.

The hardware transfer initializer marks the programmed path inactive, resets controller sequencing, applies the requested transfer mode, translates the buffer start to bus address, programs length, enables the floppy channel, and reports success. A build-time sanity option additionally rejects ranges that straddle the sixty-four-kilobyte boundary with a diagnostic.

A two-entry dispatch vector abstracts DMA operations behind request, release, residue query, memory allocation, and transfer setup hooks. The first entry binds the hardware implementations while the second binds the emulated implementations, with selection driven by the virtual-mode flag.
Default controller bases and population limits are fixed facts: primary base 0x3f0, secondary -1, controller count 2, drive count 8, with an empty extra-parameter hook.

Reads of the floppy type nibbles from a fixed real-time clock location acquire the RTC spin protection with interrupt state preserved and release it afterwards. Drive zero uses the high nibble and drive one uses the low nibble.
The ISA translation helper returns the bus address corresponding to a kernel virtual pointer by applying the physical translation and narrowing to the bus width.

Kernel floating-point availability is constantly reported present. The begin wrapper requests initialization of the vector control register alone on sixty-four-bit builds and requests both legacy and vector initialization on thirty-two-bit builds.
Floating-point register sections suppress bottom-half handling on conventional builds and suppress preemption on fully preemptible real-time builds, with symmetric restore on exit.
State release and guest extended-disable notification plus exit synchronization are defined as empty operations. A separate setter marks guest state confidential and a predicate reports that mark.

During task switch the previous task keeps its registers untouched when it already awaits reload, lacks floating-point support, or is a kernel or worker thread. Otherwise the path flags the task for reload, preserves registers into its state, records the current processor to permit same-processor restore elision, and emits a deactivation trace.
Each task carries its floating-point container immediately beyond the end of the task descriptor in memory.

The legacy save image holds control, status, tag, instruction and operand address components, room for eight extended-precision registers, and a software-only status field that hardware save leaves untouched.

The extended save image starts with narrow control, status, tag, and opcode fields, continues with an address representation that can appear either as wide instruction and data pointers or as offset plus selector pairs, then vector control plus mask, then space for legacy registers and vector registers, closing with padding and a software-reserved alternative view, aligned to sixteen bytes.
MXCSR reset value is 0x1f80 and the combined MXCSR plus flags coverage is eight bytes.

The software emulation image mirrors the legacy header and register file and appends stack-top indication, change and lookahead markers, update suppression, arithmetic mode, access limit, a pointer to emulation context, and a return address.

Feature indices order legacy floating-point first and vector second, then extended features from YMM onward through APX with reserved slots and a terminal count, and the first extended index equals YMM.

Each named feature owns a single-bit mask derived from its index. Two composites are defined: one joining legacy floating-point with vector, another joining opmask with both ZMM portions. Tile coverage joins data with configuration when enabled and is zero otherwise.

Fixed-width wrappers provide storage for sixteen, thirty-two, sixty-four byte registers and a kilobyte tile row. Upper YMM halves, bound register pairs and quadruples, bound control pairs with a sixty-four-byte padded form are built from those primitives with packed layout.
Vector extension state comprises eight opmask entries, sixteen upper ZMM slices, sixteen high ZMM registers, and a protection-key value with padding, all packed.

Control-flow state holds user settings with shadow-stack pointer and three supervisor pointers. Branch-record state holds control, depth, last-exception triple, and a flexible tail of from, to, and info triples.

Tile configuration holds eight control words and tile data holds one kilobyte row. Additional packed state carries sixteen extended general registers and a single address-space identifier. The save header records present features, compaction flags, and reserved words.
The compacted-format indicator is bit sixty-three of the compaction bitmap and the guest permission lock occupies bit sixty-three of the permission word.

The full save area chains the extended image, the header, and a flexible extended region with sixty-four-byte alignment. A page-sized union offers legacy, extended, software, and full views. The state descriptor records kernel and user sizes, sized and user-visible feature sets, trapped features, allocation, guest, confidentiality, and use flags, ending with the register union which must remain last and sixty-four-byte aligned.

The per-task container tracks last processor, vector-use timestamp, active and inactive state pointers, thread and guest permission records, and inline initial state that must remain last. Guest descriptors track enabled features, error value, user size, and state pointer. System and virtual-processor configuration records capture maximum and default sizes with maximum, default, legacy, and independently managed feature sets. Permission records hold the master bitmap plus kernel and user sizes, with sizes valid only under signal-handler protection and direct bitmap access discouraged.
FXSAVE length is 512, header length is 64 at offset 512, YMM length is 256 at offset 576, required alignment is 64, and the extend mask excludes legacy floating-point, vector, and the top bit.

User-supported coverage joins floating-point, vector, YMM, opmask, both ZMM parts, protection keys, both bound parts, tile, and APX. Restore coverage removes protection keys. Dynamic coverage equals tile data alone. Guest supervisor coverage equals kernel CET alone. Supervisor-supported coverage joins PASID, user CET, and guest supervisor. Independent coverage equals branch records alone. Supervisor-unsupported coverage equals tracing alone.
Extended control register zero selects the enabled-feature mask and register one selects the in-use mask.
One helper writes a sixty-four-bit value to the indexed control register by splitting low and high halves, while another helper returns the current in-use feature set.

Each examined header defines a once-only inclusion guard. Active extended register queries alias the floating-point register-set predicate, and IA32 signal structures alias their generic counterparts.

Crossing a sixty-four-kilobyte boundary or using high or out-of-range buffers forces the emulated DMA path, and low versus high memory demand different release paths. Trailing floating-point state is dynamically sized so nothing may follow the register union or inline state. Confidential guest state carries no salvageable register content yet its descriptor must exist to sustain preemption and soft-interrupt floating-point use.

Callable entry helpers include bus translation, DMA mode selection with both hardware and emulated setup, kernel floating-point begin, register-section lock pair, task-switch deactivation, and control-register write plus in-use query.
